objectives: Say what please and thank you are for.
Ask for something politely with please.
Say thank you when somebody helps you or gives you something.
Use please and thank you with grown-ups, friends, and shopkeepers.
Know what to do when you forget to say them.
Be kind to somebody who is shy.

sections.body:
Please and thank you are only two words. They are short. But they change how a person feels.

**Please** is the word you use before you ask for something. You say *please* when you want a toy, when you want food, when you want to go out, and when you want help with something.

**Thank you** is the word you use after you get what you wanted, or after somebody helps you. You say *thank you* when your friend shares with you, when a grown-up gives you water, and when the shopkeeper hands you your bag.

Both words are magic because of what they say underneath. Please says: *I am not taking it. I am asking.* Thank you says: *I noticed what you did. It helped me.*

When you use them, people are happy to do things for you. A child who says please gets helped faster. A child who says thank you makes grown-ups smile. And that is not just for grown-ups. It works with your friends too.

Learning to say please and thank you is a skill, like tying your shoes. Nobody is born knowing it. You practise it, and one day it comes by itself.

In this book you will learn the exact moments to use each word, what to do when you forget, and how to be kind to a friend who is too shy to speak.
examples: Please, may I have some water?
Can I please play with you?
sections.heading: Two small words that make people happy

sections.body:
You say **please** whenever you are asking for something you do not have right now. It is the little signal that says *I am asking, not taking*.

Say please when you want food. *Please, I am hungry.* Say please when you want to borrow. *Please can I use your pencil?* Say please when you want help. *Please, I cannot reach it.*

Say please when you want to go somewhere. *Please, can we go to the park?* Say please when you want to play with somebody. *Please, can I join the game?*

There is one more please that many people forget. Say it when you are **offering** something too. *Please, take this.* And say it when you are **taking** something. *Please, may I have one?* The word is about sharing, not only about asking.

Look at the person when you say it. A please said to a person is much warmer than a please shouted at a room.

And if the answer is no, thank the person anyway for listening. *Thanks for saying no.* That is being polite about a no.
examples: Please, may I have an apple?
Please, I am stuck on this zip.
Please, take my seat by the window.
sections.heading: When to say please

sections.body:
Grown-ups use a few polite words a lot. Here they are, one by one.

**Please** is the word before a request. It makes asking soft and friendly instead of pushy.

**Thank you** is the word after you get help or a gift. It tells the person their kindness was noticed.

**Sorry** is the word when you did something wrong or hurt somebody. Sorry means you take responsibility. Sorry without *but* works best. *Sorry I pushed you* is better than *sorry but you were in the way*.

**Excuse me** is the polite way to get somebody's attention or to pass by them. You say it before you interrupt an adult who is busy.

**May I** is a very polite way to ask. *May I go to the toilet?* sounds careful and grown-up. Children who use *may I* are usually listened to.

**After you** is what you say when somebody else gets there first. It is a small way of being fair.

When you do not know what to say, please and thank you will always do.
examples: Excuse me, where is the toilet?

sections.body:
Asking nicely is a small routine. Learn it once and it works everywhere.

First, get close and look at the person. Do not shout across the room.

Next, wait a moment. If the person is busy talking, wait until they stop. Then ask.

Then ask with your please. Use a calm voice. A soft voice says *I respect you*.

After that, wait for the answer. Do not ask again straight away. Give the person a second.

If the answer is yes, say thank you. If the answer is no, say thank you too. It was not rude to ask.

And if you got upset while waiting, that is normal. Say *I will wait until you are finished* and come back later.
examples: Please, can I have my turn?
I will wait until you finish.
sections.heading: How to ask nicely, step by step
steps: Go to the person and look at them.
Wait until they are not busy.
Ask with please in a calm voice.
Say thank you, whatever the answer is.

sections.body:
Some children find it hard to speak to new people. That is called being shy. It is not rudeness.

Do not laugh at a shy friend. Do not talk for them. Give them time.

You can help in small ways. Walk with them. Start the game for them. Say *I am going to ask her, do you want to come with me?*

If they want to practise, practise with them first. Say please and thank you together until it feels easy.

And sometimes you can speak for them gently. *She wants to join too, if that is okay.* Then the shy friend gets a turn without having to do all of it alone.

Kindness is not about being loud. It is about noticing somebody.
examples: Do you want to come and say hello with me?
I will ask first, and you can follow.
Take your time. There is no hurry.
sections.heading: Helping a shy friend to be polite too

sections.body:
You will forget. Everybody forgets. Grown-ups forget to say please sometimes.

The good news is that you can fix it later. If you forgot to say please, go back and say it now. *Sorry, I forgot to say please.*

If you forgot to say thank you, go and find the person. *Thank you for the book. I am sorry I did not say it sooner.* Most people will be happy to hear it, even if it is a day later.

A small thank you late is better than no thank you at all. Try it and see.

You can also say thank you without words. A smile does it. A wave does it. Helping them carry something does it. But the word is still the best.

And if somebody is unkind to you, you do not have to be polite about it. Say *no* in a strong voice, walk away, and tell a grown-up. Being polite never means being pushed around.
examples: Sorry, I forgot to say please.
Thank you for waiting for me.
No. I do not want to play that.
sections.heading: What to do when you forget

item.summary: Please and thank you are two small words that make people happy. After reading this you can ask for things politely, say thank you at the right moment, and help other people feel good too.
